statute.alkoholilaki.label: Alcohol Act, section 20
statute.alkoholilaki.note: A licence holder can serve in an approved space if it has been notified at least three days before. There's no statutory processing time for a new temporary licence, so apply right away.
statute.avioliittolaki.label: Marriage Act, sections 11 and 13
statute.avioliittolaki.note: The certificate is issued no earlier than the seventh day after the request, and the wedding must take place within four months. So request it no earlier than four months and no later than about two weeks before the wedding.
statute.kokoontumislaki.label: Assembly Act, section 14
statute.kokoontumislaki.note: The police must be notified at least five days before the event. A small event that needs no order, safety or traffic arrangements needs no notification. The law sets no headcount.
statute.pelastuslaki.label: Rescue Act, section 16, and Government Decree 407/2011, section 3
statute.pelastuslaki.note: A rescue plan must be submitted to the fire and rescue service at least 14 days before the event if 200 or more people are present at once. The same applies to open flames, pyrotechnics and unusually difficult evacuation.
statute.ysl.label: Environmental Protection Act, section 118
statute.ysl.note: A noise notification goes to the municipal environmental authority at least 30 days before the event if the noise can be expected to be particularly disturbing. The municipality's own regulations can shorten the time or remove the requirement. Private individuals' own parties are exempt.

why.P-30: If the event needs traffic controllers or temporary security staff, notify the police at least two weeks before. For a large or multi-day event, contact the police department where the event is held early in the planning. Talking about safety in good time avoids surprises on both sides.
why.SU-01: Disposable waste is the biggest single job at clean-up.
why.SU-02: The food is already paid for. With a plan, it doesn't get binned in the rush.
why.SU-03: Tap water is free, bottled water isn't.
why.SU-04: Sorted waste is cheaper to dispose of, and many venues require it.
why.SU-05: The deposits often cover the clean-up crew's coffee.
why.SU-06: Bought decor ends up in someone's home or the bin afterwards.
why.SU-07: Fewer questions and fewer cars at the door.
why.SU-08: An unposted poster is a wasted print bill.
why.SU-09: Unsold merch is money sitting in storage.
why.SU-10: One van is cheaper than three taxis.
why.SU-11: Tech left on overnight is a classic cause of disputes with the venue.
why.SU-12: They work for the next event, and new ones cost money.
why.SU-13: Vegetarian food suits most diets and cuts down on special orders.
why.SU-14: Grant makers, the city and partners ask for these in the next application.
why.SU-15: No taxi bills and no one late for soundcheck.
why.SU-99: This one's a joke. If a funder actually asks for an emissions report, ask them which calculator they use.

why.locked: Only the organiser can do this
why.noVenueSecurity: The venue doesn't handle security because no venue contact is on site.
why.policeEarly: This is a large, multi-day event, so contact the police now.
why.policeTwoWeeks: Outdoor events often need traffic controllers, so the notice goes in two weeks before.
